messages:
alex cho: noticed another prod OOM on shard-a around 04:12 UTC, saw kv-cache memory keep climbing after warmup. stack looks like cache growth + fragmented slabs

maria hsiao: ugh. thanks for flagging. can you paste the pprof snapshot and the allocation heatmap?

alex cho: pasted below. small snippet from pprof top: 
```
# pprof --text kv-cache.prod.heap.2026-03-22.pb
  42.3%  42.3%  runtime.mallocgc
  28.1%  70.4%  github.com/redwood/kv.(*Cache).Put
  14.6%  85.0%  github.com/redwood/storage.(*Shard).loadSegments
```

kevin nguyen: looks like repeated small allocations from Put path. could be duplicate indexing causing retention. also fragmentation metric spiked in the same window.

samir patel: infra-bot created incident 1977754321-kv-oom-shard-a, link: https://redwood.incidents/1977754321

infra-bot: Incident 1977754321 created. Priority: P1 (OOM), assigned: eng-runtime oncall.

maria hsiao: propose immediate actions:
- A1: add temporary per-shard hard cap to KV cache (owner: kevin) - ETA 24h
- A2: capture continuous heap profiles at 30s during peak for 48h (owner: alex) - ETA 2h
- A3: run fragmentation GC after every N writes as a stopgap (owner: samir) - ETA 12h
- A4: add alert for sustained cache growth > 5%/5m (owner: maria) - ETA 6h

kevin nguyen: will try cap + check regression tests for throughput. plan: conservative cap to avoid tail latencies, roll canary 1% then 10% if stable.

alex cho: starting profiler now. uploading continuous traces to /s3/oom-investigations/1977754321/

samir patel: for fragmentation GC, we need perf-proof: I'll prototype a background compaction job and benchmark on staging. If we see >10% improvement drop fragmentation we can promote.

maria hsiao: owner checkpoints - please post short status updates in this thread when you hit each milestone. I'll keep the postmortem follow-up doc updated: https://docs.redwood/eng-runtime/kv-oom-postmortem-followup

kevin nguyen: quick note - if cap causes cache misses to spike, fallback policy -> route to secondary replica (config: routing.fallback.secondary=true). I'll add instrumentation to measure miss rate.

alex cho: initial 30s profiler shows 3 hotspots in Put: key serializing, value copy, and segment chain growth. copying is expensive for big values (200-500kb). I'll add zero-copy path to the hot path as an experiment. ETA 3d for safe rollout.

maria hsiao: risk log: recurring incidents pattern: similar OOMs in last 6 weeks but different triggers (frag GC, ghost-allocs, large payloads). we should track this as a recurring class, add recurrence tag on the incident.

samir patel: agree. proposed long-term work: A-LT1: refactor cache to support slab allocator + reuse arenas (owner: samir, kevin) - ETA 6w; A-LT2: KV compaction strategy + metrics (owner: kevin) - ETA 4w; A-LT3: add synthetic load that reproduces fragmentation on CI (owner: alex) - ETA 2w.

maria hsiao: logging owners & timelines in follow-up doc. I'll schedule a 30m retro in 7 days to reassess and close action items.

alex cho: quick status update - profiler uploaded, initial cap patch in review (PR #4218).

kevin nguyen: cap PR merged to canary, enabling at 1% now. will monitor memory and miss-rate dashboards.

maria hsiao: thanks. if anyone notices side effects, ping @oncall and post here. adding weekly reminder: "kv-memory-trend-check" to make sure we catch slow regressions.

alex cho: noted. leaving detailed heap diffs in /s3 path and adding a small repro harness to my branch.

samir patel: setting up staging compaction benchmark tonight. will post numbers here by EOD PT.

maria hsiao: excellent. summary for follow-up doc: A1(kevin,24h), A2(alex,2h), A3(samir,12h), A4(maria,6h), LT1(samir+kevin,6w), LT2(kevin,4w), LT3(alex,2w). will update incident and send calendar invite for retro. :white_check_mark:

kevin nguyen: noted. any objections to keeping this thread as the canonical action-tracking channel for this incident?

maria hsiao: no objections. locking actions here.

alex cho: thanks everyone. I'll post profiler diffs once I finish initial analysis.

samir patel: EOD update: staging compaction reduced fragmentation metric from 0.42 -> 0.28 in benchmark, preliminary.

maria hsiao: great progress. closing for now, will reopen if new signals appear.
